body:
THE OWNER SAYS WE DO NOT NEED TO HAND-AUTHOR A STORY -- GENERATE ONE, OR USE ONE FOUND ONLINE. HE IS RIGHT, AND THE ARCHITECTURE FOR IT ALREADY EXISTS. I framed hand-authoring as the only alternative an hour ago and that was wrong.

WHAT THE COMPILER ACTUALLY WANTS, measured -- NarrativeCompilerInput.of takes:

  source        StorySource            the text
  atlas         SurfaceAtlas           sentence and token segmentation
  localCharts   PropositionEvidence    per surface unit
  evidence, situations, contexts, summary, memberships, causal    -- ALL "Attempt" TYPES
  policy, receipt, provenance

IT TAKES ATTEMPTS, NOT ANSWERS. SituationAttempt, ContextAssignmentAttempt, StorySummaryAttempt, SegmentMembershipAttempt, CausalAttempt. The compiler ADJUDICATES proposals and may refuse them. That is exactly the shape a generator feeds.

AND acquire ALREADY HAS THE WHOLE PROPOSAL PIPELINE: task, prompt, proposal, critic, foil, patch, resolve, orchestrate, cache. AgentProposal[A], PromptPackageManifest, ProposalDisposition, EvidenceRef, ConflictTarget. THE ACQUISITION FRAMEWORK IS BUILT. What is missing is a provider that emits attempts.

SO THE 1526 LINES OF WarOfTheGhostsModel.scala ARE NOT "A MODEL SOMEONE WROTE". THEY ARE THE ATTEMPTS, WRITTEN BY HAND. A generator proposes the same things; the compiler and critics do the same adjudication either way.

THREE ROUTES, cheapest first:

  1. SYNTHETIC MODEL, NO TEXT AND NO LLM. CodecGens.scala:574 already builds a
     StoryModel[Validated] programmatically. Promote a generator into main scope and Edition.build
     has a second value to render TODAY. Answers "is the renderer general" and nothing else.

  2. PUBLIC-DOMAIN TEXT + GENERATED ATTEMPTS. A found story gives `source` for free and `atlas` is
     mechanical. An LLM proposes the attempts; acquire's critics and foils check them; the compiler
     accepts or refuses. THIS IS THE LLM ACQUISITION ADAPTER README SAYS WE LACK, and it is the same
     work as Stage 1b rather than a detour around it.

  3. HAND-AUTHORED SECOND STORY. Days. Worst option and I should not have led with it.

TWO CONSTRAINTS THAT MUST TRAVEL WITH ROUTE 2.

  LICENSING: use PUBLIC DOMAIN only. Bartlett's own sources, Aesop, folk tales, Boas -- WOG itself
  comes from Boas. That avoids the owner's standing rule entirely: anything behind an access
  agreement is the owner's to obtain, and nobody accepts terms on his behalf. A public-domain story
  needs no agreement from anyone.

  AND THE ONE THAT MATTERS MORE: A GENERATED MODEL IS NOT A RESEARCHER-REVIEWED FIXTURE, AND THE TWO
  MUST NOT BECOME INDISTINGUISHABLE. WOG carries twelve plain-language expectations a human wrote
  and checked; the docs call it "a researcher-reviewed fixture". An LLM-proposed model that passes
  the compiler has passed VALIDATION, not REVIEW. If both end up as `StoryModel[Validated]` with
  nothing separating them, we have built exactly the defect we spent today naming -- a value that
  cannot be told apart from a different value it must be told apart from. Whatever route 2 produces
  must carry its provenance in a form that survives into every downstream receipt.

RECOMMENDATION: route 1 this week to answer the renderer question, route 2 as the real programme,
and route 3 never.
